title: Lightweight telemetry demultiplexer for inference micro-batches
creator: Priya Nair
description: Background: As inference requests are increasingly micro-batched at the serving runtime, we need a lightweight component that can demultiplex per-request telemetry (latency, error counts, token-counts, model-variant labels) from aggregated micro-batch metrics so that downstream SLOs/alerts and cost attributions remain accurate without exploding cardinality. Existing OTLP producers at the runtime emit batch-level envelopes and the Prometheus bridge currently scrapes only aggregated counters. This ticket proposes a small telemetry demultiplexer (sidecar/collector component) that reconstructs per-request KPI envelopes from micro-batch telemetry, attaches tracing/span correlation metadata, applies adaptive sampling and label normalization, and exports both Prometheus-compatible timeseries (remote_write or exposition) and OTLP envelopes for long-term storage.
background_details: Problems observed: 1) Alerts and SLOs on per-route P95 are noisy because micro-batch aggregation hides individual slow requests. 2) Billing attribution needs per-request token counts but current exporter only emits batch sums. 3) Tenant cardinality spikes when per-request keys are naively materialized. 4) We also need a stable correlation from traces -> metrics for root-cause workflows. Goals: - Recreate per-request KPI envelopes with bounded label sets. - Preserve trace/span correlation (trace_id, span_id, request_id) in outputs. - Ensure CPU/memory cost of the demux is small and scalable on Dedicated nodes. - Output both Prometheus-friendly metrics and OTLP envelopes to enable short-term alerting + long-term analytics.
proposal: Build a small Go-based Otel Collector processor extension (telemetry-demux) that runs as a sidecar alongside serving processes. It will: 1) receive batch-level OTLP metrics and the batch's request roster (light roster metadata emitted by the runtime), 2) reconstruct per-request envelopes by distributing samples according to the roster and per-request hooks (when explicit per-request stats exist use them), 3) apply label canonicalization and cardinality caps (tenant, route, model, model_variant, region), 4) run adaptive sampling: keep all_error=true samples, deterministically sample low-impact successful requests using hashing on request_id to a target sample rate configurable by route, 5) emit Prometheus metrics (histogram buckets or exemplars for latency) plus OTLP envelopes sent to our metrics lake. Backward compatibility: when roster metadata missing, fall back to best-effort batching semantics and emit an aggregate metric with a special label microbatch_unresolved=true.
design_notes: - Correlation: include trace_id and span_id as exemplars on Prometheus histograms and attach as attributes on OTLP MetricData points. - Cardinality: only allow up to 6 dynamic label dimensions; map high-cardinality attributes into a bucketing label (eg. user_tier_bucket). - Sampling policy: route-configurable in Console; defaults: errors=100%, p95 candidates=5%, success=1% hashed. - Performance: keep demux in-memory with streaming decomposition (no materialization of whole batches), use object pools and a small scratch buffer to avoid GC spikes. - Failure modes: if demux fails, metrics pipeline should fall back to emitting original batch-level metric with label demux_fallback=true. - Observability for the demux itself: expose its own Prometheus metrics (processing_time_seconds, reconstructed_envelopes_total, sampled_envelopes_total, fallback_count_total).
acceptance_criteria: Per-request KPI envelopes reconstructed for >=95% of micro-batches in the canary fleet without exceeding 15% CPU overhead on the node
Prometheus histograms include exemplars with trace_id/span_id for sampled requests in canary traces
Adaptive sampling respects route-configured rates and keeps cardinality within configured caps (test tenant exhibits no new unique label explosion)
Fallback behavior validated: when roster metadata is absent, batch-level metric with microbatch_unresolved=true is emitted and downstream consumers are not broken
End-to-end dashboard (Grafana) shows reconstructed p50/p95/p99 and token-cost attribution matching ground-truth within 5% for test traces
Documentation and runbook added with rollback steps and alert thresholds

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: High cardinality leading to Prometheus churn. Mitigation: enforce label caps and transform rare values into buckets; also use exemplars instead of unique labels where possible.

Risk: Latency overhead on hot serving paths if roster emission is synchronous. Mitigation: make roster emission async and use a bounded queue; measure impact and add backpressure to runtime if needed.

Risk: Incorrect reconstruction causing billing errors. Mitigation: run thorough A/B reconciliation against ground-truth billing exporter and enable strict checks during canary; roll back if discrepancy >5%.
Risk: OTLP/Prometheus schema incompatibilities. Mitigation: add schema validation step and a compatibility layer that emits a fallback aggregate metric when mapping fails.
